definition: Purine and pyrimidine nucleotides and their direct precursors.
Proteinogenic amino acids and the branchpoint intermediates of their families.
Neutral single sugars, including pentoses, hexoses and deoxyhexoses.
Nitrogen-bearing sugars such as N-acetylglucosamine and sialic acid.
Sugar acids such as glucuronate and galacturonate.
Glycan polymers and the decorations attached to them.
Proteins and the peptides released from them.

Converts an acquired substrate into central carbon metabolism.
Moves a substrate across the cell boundary.
Acts on dietary plant polysaccharides or the sugars released from them.
Acts on host-derived glycans or the sugars released from them.

A peptide or heterogeneous peptide mixture released by proteolytic cleavage of a protein.
A single sugar or sugar acid.
Any other boundary metabolite, including phosphorylated intermediates.

An inorganic nutrient.

Not itself a biomass building block.

A structure built within the cell envelope itself rather than projecting from it.
A machine whose curated architecture exists to translocate substrates across the envelope.

A receptor-array signalling pathway with a coupled kinase, a diffusible response regulator and a receptor methylation adaptation cycle.
